messages:
Alex (Support): Iris in EU-WEST reporting a sudden spike in 5xx from the hosted API. Started ~2026-05-12T12:03Z. customer_id=acct_89a2. Payloads: generation requests returning 503 and 502 intermittently. example body: `{"error":"auth: session lookup timed out"}`. Can someone take a look? cc @Maya (Oncall)
Maya (Oncall): on it. Can you paste a raw request/response sample + any request_id? Severity: P1 for the customer?
Alex (Support): Severity P1 from customer. Request sample below (redacted):
```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_redacted" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"g-4o","input":"short prompt"}'
```
Response: `HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable`
Body: `{"error":"auth: session lookup timed out"}`
request_id header: `req_20260512_az7f3`
ops-bot: INCIDENT CREATED INC-2026-1267 (auto-alert from control-plane healthcheck)
Priya (Eng-SRE): seeing matching spikes in control-plane logs and config-db latency graphs. Quick triage: there are repeated timeouts to config-db (~504 from DB proxy) and routing-policy service returning 502 when it can't read policies. Pod restarts for `routing-policy` around 12:01-12:04 UTC. Also auth-service logs show `session lookup error: context deadline exceeded`.
Tom (Platform): we had a routing-policy change rolled out at 11:58 that changed policy cache invalidation frequency (smaller TTL). Could be causing higher DB read QPS. I'm reverting that rollout now.
Iris (Customer): thanks. repro steps from our side: we run a burst test hitting 40 rps, about ~15% of requests see 502/503 intermittently. We sent request_id `req_20260512_az7f3` and attached logs.
Priya (Eng-SRE): digging deeper: metrics snapshot:
- config-db p99 read latency before: ~20ms, after 11:58: p99 -> ~420ms
- config-db connection queue length spiked from 2 -> 140
- routing-policy pods OOM/restart count: 3/3 on eu-west cluster
Hypothesis: cache TTL reduction caused synchronous reads to config-db to spike, exhausting connection pool and causing auth session lookups to time out.
Maya (Oncall): what's immediate mitigation? Customer is in production and reporting errors.
Priya (Eng-SRE): mitigation plan (2-step):
1) Emergency rollback / revert TTL change (Tom is on it).
2) Enable routing-policy fallback to cached policy when DB read fails. We have a runtime flag `policy.fallback_on_db_error=true` that returns last-known policy. Apply to eu-west.
Applying fallback flag now with k8s patch:```bash
kubectl -n controlplane set env deployment/routing-policy POLICY_FALLBACK_ON_DB_ERROR=true --record
kubectl rollout restart deployment/routing-policy -n controlplane
```
Priya (Eng-SRE): also temporarily increase config-db connection limit on the DB proxy and add a connection queue to smooth bursts. Commands (DB admin):```sql
-- on proxy config
set max_connections = 1000;
reload proxy;
```
Tom (Platform): rollback deployed (confirmed). TTL change reverted at 12:07 UTC. Restarted 2/3 routing-policy pods; one pod still in CrashLoop, investigating image vs OOM. Restarted successfully at 12:10.
ops-bot: ALERT SUPPRESSED for INC-2026-1267 (auto)
Priya (Eng-SRE): after rollback + fallback flag, error rate dropped to ~0.5% from 15% within 3m. DB p99 falling back to ~50ms. We're keeping the fallback flag for 1h while load normalizes.
Alex (Support): updated customer: temporary mitigation applied, engineering investigating root cause and next steps. Customer wants RCA and ETA for full fix.
Iris (Customer): thanks, we see much fewer 5xx now. Can you confirm whether any requests were reprocessed or lost?
Maya (Oncall): no request reprocessing; fallback serves cached policy so responses are still generated by model backend. No customer data was leaked. We're only serving last-known routing policy which may route to slightly different model variants in rare cases.
Priya (Eng-SRE): root cause suspected: config change to routing-policy TTL + missing DB connection capacity for bursty workloads. Action items:
- revert TTL permanently and re-evaluate cache sizing (assigned Tom)
- increase DB proxy connection pool and add load-shedding threshold (assigned Priya)
- postmortem with timeline + customer impact (assigned Maya)
Ticket: case_20260512_4532 created for the account, linked to INC-2026-1267.
Tom (Platform): created PR to add a circuit-breaker in routing-policy to return cached policy when DB latency crosses 200ms. Will target a staged rollout next week with canary.
Priya (Eng-SRE): for follow-up: collect sampling of affected request_ids, attach control-plane traces, and correlate with DB proxy logs. I'll export traces for the window 11:55-12:15 UTC.
Alex (Support): recorded repro, mitigation, and next steps in the support case. Will share postmortem draft with customer once ready.
Iris (Customer): appreciate the fast response, please keep us posted.
Maya (Oncall): closing this thread for now. If errors resurface, reopen or ping me directly. (reaction :thumbsup:)
